q1_issues.issue: Both sealed Implication rules use the variable $x inside one stored term, violating the requirement that every sealed rule get fresh variables shared with no other conjunct of that seal (variables must not co-vary inside one term).

The additive "more" is dropped from both counts — "nine MORE people had died" and "160 MORE were infected" become plain (Cardinality … 9) / (Cardinality … 160), losing the incremental-to-a-running-total reading the sentence states.

q2_gaps: "N more" — an incremental / additive count relative to a prior total has no licensed carrier (Cardinality states the size of that group, not an increment)
a numeral with an elided head noun ("160 more [people]") — one-anaphora covers "one", but there is no rule for recovering the head kind for a bare numeral
notes: (Member sars virus) is licensed because the anaphoric definite "the virus" supplies the kind word for SARS, and projecting only the named referent's Name/typing out of the say-seal is correct. The same causal participant is encoded two ways — (From sk_die_1 sars) vs (Instrument sk_infect_1 sars) — each defensible under its own preposition rule, but the two records will not unify.
